articles.title: Kauvery Hospital, The Hindu to organise webinar on post-partum care - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kauvery Hospital and The Hindu are hosting a webinar on "Post-partum Care for Mothers" to commemorate Mother's Day. The session, moderated by journalist Soma Basu, will feature K. Thendral, Clinical Lead and Senior Consultant, Obstetrics and Gynaecology at Kauvery Hospital, Radial Road; P. Sathya Sudhakar, Consultant Obstetrician and Gynaecologist at Kauvery Hospital Salem; and Manjeswari G., Psychologist and Sexual Health Therapist at Maa Kauvery, Trichy.  The webinar will be held on May 8th at 11:30 a.m. and registration is available through the link https://newsth.live/ THKMOE.

articles.title: Cook more at home to reduce ultra-processed food intake, say cardiologist groups | Ultra-processed foods | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Doctors and the European Society of Cardiology and European Association of Preventive Cardiology have issued a clinical consensus statement urging cardiologists to advise patients on reducing their intake of ultra-processed foods (UPFs). The recommendations include encouraging home cooking, avoiding late eating, choosing high-fiber minimally processed foods, and practicing mindful eating.  The statement emphasizes the importance of visual reminders for patients when discussing UPF consumption, particularly in relation to heart disease risk factors like blood pressure and weight gain.

articles.title: Argentina investigates link to deadly hantavirus outbreak on cruise ship | Health News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Argentina's health ministry is investigating a possible link between the deadly hantavirus outbreak on an Atlantic cruise ship and their country. The investigation will involve capturing and testing rodents in areas frequented by the Dutch couple who died from the virus, as well as sending diagnostic materials to laboratories in several countries. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus confirmed eight suspected cases of the hantavirus, with three confirmed deaths.  The cruise ship, which departed for Spain on Wednesday after evacuating three passengers, remains under close monitoring by health authorities.

articles.title: Hantavirus-hit cruise ship leaves Cape Verde after three evacuated
articles.rephrased_article: A Dutch cruise ship, the MV Hondius, carrying 146 passengers from 23 countries, has left Cape Verde after three people were medically evacuated for hantavirus treatment. The World Health Organization (WHO) and Oceanwide Expeditions, the ship's operator, are working to confirm if other passengers have contracted the virus.  The ship will travel to the Canary Islands where all remaining passengers will undergo medical assessments upon arrival.

articles.title: Three evacuated from hantavirus-hit ship as Spain says vessel can dock | Hantavirus | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, director general of the World Health Organization (WHO), coordinated the evacuation of three people with suspected hantavirus from a Dutch-flagged cruise ship, the MV Hondius. The passengers, including a British doctor and two other crew members, were transported to the Netherlands for medical care.  The ship's operator, Oceanwide Expeditions, is working with authorities in Spain and the Canary Islands to determine the next steps for the vessel and its passengers.

articles.title: Canary Islands refuses to allow MV Hondius with hantavirus to dock | Health News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Canary Islands have refused to allow the luxury cruise ship MV Hondius, carrying passengers with a suspected hantavirus outbreak, to dock at any of its ports.  Despite Spain's agreement for docking, Fernando Clavijo, president of the Canary Islands, cited insufficient information about the outbreak as the reason for his decision. The WHO has identified eight cases linked to the ship, including three confirmed infections and five suspected cases, with three passengers already deceased.

articles.title: How hunger rewires the biology of an entire generation | Hunger | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Al Jazeera reports that a new study published in the journal "Nature" reveals how chronic hunger can alter the biology of an entire generation. The research, conducted by scientists at Harvard University, found that prolonged food insecurity can impact brain development and increase susceptibility to various health problems.

articles.title: Hantavirus-hit cruise ship to sail to Canary Islands, passengers to undergo medical screening - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Spain has granted permission for the virus-hit cruise ship MV Hondius to sail to the Canary Islands, where passengers and crew will undergo medical screening under strict containment protocols. The decision follows Cape Verde's announcement that it lacked capacity to handle the situation.  The outbreak of Hantavirus on board has claimed three lives, including a Dutch couple and a German national, with seven cases reported by the World Health Organization (WHO).  All individuals will be examined, treated if necessary, and then repatriated to their home countries in coordination with international health agencies.

articles.title: Welfare schemes should reach the common man: Deputy CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, Deputy Chief Minister of Telangana, emphasized the importance of public interest and welfare schemes in government decisions. He urged officials to explore direct distribution of procured jowar and maize through the Public Distribution System (PDS) to avoid middlemen benefiting from open auctions.  He also directed officials to ensure nutritious food for students studying in Gurukuls and hostels belonging to SC, ST, BC, and minority communities, highlighting the state's commitment to combating malnutrition.

articles.title: Black people in England twice as likely to suffer stroke as white counterparts | Stroke | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A new study by King’s College London researchers found that people from black African and Caribbean backgrounds in England are twice as likely to experience strokes compared to their white counterparts. The analysis, based on the South London Stroke Register, also revealed a 13% increase in stroke incidence between 2020 and 2024, despite a decline in overall incidence between 1995-99 and 2010-14.  Dr Camila Pantoja-Ruiz, lead author of the study, suggests that this trend may be linked to factors like racism and socioeconomic circumstances impacting access to care. Maeva May, director of policy at the Stroke Association, emphasized the need for equitable stroke prevention efforts, highlighting the disproportionate burden on black communities due to higher rates of undetected risk factors such as high blood pressure and diabetes.

articles.title: ‘Tap water samples found to be contaminated with E. coli in Palluruthy’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala Water Authority (KWA) officials and health officials in Palluruthy are investigating the cause of 18 reported hepatitis A cases, with seven individuals still hospitalized. Initial findings indicate contamination from E. coli bacteria in water samples from infected residents' homes. While KWA denies leaks in its pipes, they attribute the issue to illegal motor pump usage by residents drawing water, leading to contaminated water entering the network. The Asian Development Bank (ADB)-funded project aims to optimize water distribution in Kochi and a year of dedicated study is planned for pipe replacement if necessary.

articles.title: State grants approval to procure six MRI machines for district hospitals - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The State government has approved the procurement of six MRI machines for district and district-level hospitals under the National Free Diagnostic Services Programme. The Mission Director, National Health Mission (NHM) submitted the proposal, which will be funded by ECRP-2 and ECRP-1 savings.  These units will be installed in Davanagere, Mysuru, Dharwad, Bagalkote, Jayanagar General/K.C. General Hospital in Bengaluru, and Bengaluru South. The procurement will be carried out through the Karnataka State Medical Supplies Corporation (KSMSC).

articles.title: FDA blocked studies finding Covid and shingles vaccines safe, HHS official says | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has withdrawn several studies that found Covid-19 and shingles vaccines to be safe, citing concerns about broad conclusions drawn from the data.  Andrew Nixon, an HHS spokesperson, stated the studies were withdrawn because they did not meet the agency's high standards of scientific integrity. Janet Woodcock, former FDA principal deputy commissioner, expressed concern over a pattern of suppressing information that supports vaccine safety. The studies, funded by taxpayer money and costing millions of dollars, examined vaccine safety in various age groups and found rare side effects.

articles.title: Unwell British crew member to be ‘urgently’ evacuated from cruise ship after hantavirus cases | Infectious diseases | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A British crew member and a Dutch colleague onboard the luxury cruise ship MV Hondius are being medically evacuated after experiencing respiratory symptoms suspected to be hantavirus.  The World Health Organization (WHO) has prioritized their care, with Spain receiving the ship in three or four days for medical examination and treatment of all passengers and crew. The Spanish health ministry confirmed it will receive the ship in the Canary Islands where medical teams will examine and treat those onboard. A British passenger who was medically evacuated to South Africa is improving while two others remain on board awaiting evacuation.

articles.title: US to take steps to curb antidepressant prescribing, RFK Jr says | Robert F Kennedy Jr | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Robert F Kennedy Jr., the former Trump administration’s health secretary, announced a plan by the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to curb antidepressant use in the US. The plan aims to promote deprescribing when clinically indicated and increase access to non-medication options for treating depression, including psychotherapy, diet, physical activity, and social connection. The HHS also provided guidance to mental health practitioners on managing the process of deprescribing and emphasized the importance of evidence-based care.  The American Psychiatric Association supported the administration's plans but expressed concerns about oversimplifying the mental health crisis and called for solutions that address workforce shortages, limited access to care, and uneven distribution of care.

articles.title: Philip Morris uses secret Senate hearing to warn illegal tobacco in Australia could wipe out legal trade by 2030 | Health | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Philip Morris, a tobacco giant, told a closed-door Senate hearing that soaring illegal cigarette trade would wipe out legal products in Australia by 2030. The company argued for lower federal tobacco excise to undercut hidden market operators, but Labor, the Greens, and the federal government criticized the committee chair's decision to hold the private session.  Julian Hill, the federal customs minister, called for transparency from tobacco manufacturers regarding illicit tobacco sales and supply chains, while Mark Butler, the health minister, urged MPs to adhere to WHO guidelines on engagement with tobacco companies.

articles.title: Nearly 20,000 patients ‘missing’ after initiating treatment at HIV centres, NA committee told - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The National Assembly’s Standing Committee on Health held a meeting to address the rising trend of HIV and AIDS cases in Pakistan. The committee was informed that nearly 20,000 patients who initiated treatment at ART centers for HIV/AIDS are "missing," raising concerns about follow-up, counselling, and patient retention. Health Minister Mustafa Kamal clarified that no new outbreak has occurred this year and the Global Fund is supporting Pakistan's HIV/AIDS programs. The committee also noted localized outbreaks in various regions of the country, highlighting failures in infection prevention and control measures.

articles.title: Nandyal Collector urges officials to promote online yoga classes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: District Collector Rajakumari Ganiya urged officials to promote Union AYUSH Ministry and Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga’s 100-day free online yoga classes ahead of International Yoga Day. She directed officials to share the link with government employees, their families, and the public, encouraging maximum participation in the live sessions running daily from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m., and three additional sessions between 4 p.m. and 7 p.m. The program is being organized in collaboration with ‘Habild Health Tech’.  Officials were also advised to provide medical treatment and raise awareness about traditional medical systems during public grievance redressal programs.

articles.title: Hantavirus may have spread between passengers on cruise ship, WHO says
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) is investigating a possible human-to-human transmission of hantavirus on the Dutch cruise ship MV Hondius, which has been anchored near Cape Verde. The virus, usually spread from rodents, may have spread among "really close contacts" aboard the vessel.  Medical teams from Cape Verde are assisting with the suspected cases, and testing is underway for other passengers and crew members who are displaying symptoms. Oceanwide Expeditions, the ship's operator, has confirmed that two crew members are being medically evacuated to the Netherlands while 149 people remain on board under precautionary measures. The WHO suspects the first person to fall ill could have contracted the virus before boarding the ship.

articles.title: Slow Alzheimer’s diagnoses ‘mean UK patients missing out on experimental treatments’ | Alzheimer's | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Alzheimer’s Research UK has warned that the recent surge in clinical trials for Alzheimer’s treatments is being hampered by insufficient patient participation due to delayed or inaccurate diagnoses. The charity states that too few UK patients are enrolled in trials because their diagnoses are not specific enough, potentially leaving them behind as research progresses and focuses on multiple fronts to combat the disease.  The organization emphasizes that early and accurate diagnosis is crucial for matching participants to effective treatments.

articles.title: ‘We want to go home’: US travel blogger breaks down as hantavirus outbreak kills 3 on Atlantic cruise ship - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A luxury cruise ship, the MV Hondius, carrying nearly 150 passengers and crew, has been anchored off Cape Verde after being denied permission to dock due to a suspected hantavirus outbreak. The incident began during a voyage from Argentina toward the Atlantic and Antarctic regions, resulting in three passenger deaths, including a Dutch couple and a German national. Jake Rosmarin, an American travel blogger onboard, described the situation as "very real and deeply uncertain," with passengers grappling with fear, isolation, and delayed medical evacuations.  Authorities are investigating whether the outbreak originated onboard or during land stops in South America.

articles.title: As summer approaches, skin diseases spread through Gaza’s refugee camps | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: UNRWA has warned of a growing public health crisis in Gaza, with skin diseases spreading rapidly among the displaced population. The UN agency reports that the number of skin infections has tripled in recent months due to rising temperatures, overcrowding, and sanitation issues. UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric urged for increased access to essential medical supplies, including anti-lice shampoo, lotions, hygiene supplies, pesticides, and insecticides, to prevent further harm to civilians.  The situation is particularly dire in refugee camps, where health workers are struggling to contain the spread of diseases due to shortages of materials and medications.

articles.title: ‘One meal a day with millets’ initiative launched - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research (IIMR) Director C. Tara Satyavathi urged the public to incorporate millets into their diet at least once a day for improved health outcomes.  She highlighted that National Institute of Nutrition recommendations suggest one-third of cereal consumption should be from millets, which can be included in any meal.

articles.title: UNFPA committed to supporting midwifery education, workforce development in Pakistan - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) reaffirmed its commitment to supporting Pakistan's midwifery workforce development and health systems. Dr Luay Shabaneh, UNFPA representative in Pakistan, emphasized the importance of investing in midwives as a "smart economic choice" that reduces maternal mortality and improves overall health outcomes. He highlighted the need for improved education, support, and integration of midwives into the healthcare system to ensure access to skilled care and reduce preventable deaths.  Shabaneh stressed the critical role midwives play in safeguarding mothers, newborns, and families while advocating for fair compensation, legal protection, and career advancement opportunities.

articles.title: US Supreme Court temporarily lifts ban on abortion pill mail delivery | Health News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US Supreme Court temporarily lifted a ban on mail-order delivery of the abortion pill mifepristone, restoring telehealth access for at least one week. The court's "administrative stay" was issued by Justice Samuel Alito and allows manufacturers to continue providing the medication via telemedicine and mail while legal challenges play out.  The decision comes as abortion rights remain a contentious issue in the US following the overturning of Roe v. Wade, with Democrats emphasizing access to reproductive healthcare and Republicans calling for restrictions on the procedure.

articles.title: Hantavirus scare: All you need to know about Atlantic cruise ship outbreak that killed 3 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: WHO and CDC are investigating an alleged hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise liner, which has resulted in confirmed and suspected cases among passengers. Hantavirus is a virus transmitted to humans by rodents through airborne particles from their droppings, urine, or saliva. The disease can cause serious respiratory problems, including death, and there are two main forms: hantavirus pulmonary syndrome and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome.  Early diagnosis and supportive care are crucial for managing the infection.

articles.title: Cruise ship at centre of suspected hantavirus outbreak blocked from docking in Cape Verde | Infectious diseases | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Cape Verdean officials have decided not to allow a cruise ship suspected of harboring a rare respiratory virus, the MV Hondius, to dock in their ports. The decision comes after the deaths of three passengers onboard, including a Dutch couple, and the illness of at least two others.  The World Health Organization (WHO) is investigating the outbreak, which has been linked to hantavirus, a disease primarily found in rodents.  Oceanwide Expeditions, the cruise ship operator, is working with authorities to repatriate crew members and passengers requiring medical care. The Netherlands ministry of foreign affairs is coordinating consular assistance for passengers onboard.

articles.title: Deadly Hantavirus scare on Atlantic Cruise Ship leaves 3 dead, British passenger critical | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A luxury cruise ship, the MV Hondius, travelling from Argentina to Cape Verde has been hit by a suspected hantavirus outbreak that has resulted in three deaths and several others being seriously ill. The World Health Organization (WHO) confirmed one case of hantavirus and authorities are working with South African and Dutch health officials to contain the crisis.  Authorities are coordinating efforts to evacuate affected passengers, repatriate bodies, and monitor potential exposure cases. The outbreak has raised concerns about cruise ship health risks and the difficulty in managing outbreaks in remote locations.

articles.title: Coalition accused of secretly giving big tobacco lobbyists private platform in parliament | Smoking | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Anti-smoking campaigners have accused the Coalition of secretly allowing tobacco companies to give evidence in a closed session during a parliamentary inquiry into illegal tobacco trade in Australia.  They argue this undermines public health policy and contradicts established precedent, citing concerns from Labor, the Greens, and the Australian Council on Smoking and Health. The Health Department has advised against such interactions with tobacco executives, emphasizing transparency and protection of public health policy.  The inquiry's chairwoman, Senator Leah Blyth, has been contacted for comment.

articles.title: Flaws in Kenya’s AI-driven health reforms driving up costs for the poorest | Global development | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: An investigation has revealed that a new AI-powered healthcare system in Kenya, designed to expand access to care for the country's informal workforce, is systematically overcharging the poor and undercharging the wealthy. The Social Health Authority (SHA) system uses a means-testing process based on factors like household possessions and income estimates, but has been found to be flawed and inaccurate.  This has led to widespread frustration among Kenyans, particularly those in low-income households who are struggling to afford healthcare premiums. Critics argue that the system is opaque, undermines trust in government services, and fails to accurately identify poor households. The investigation also highlights concerns about the use of proxy means testing (PMT) algorithms globally, which have been shown to be unreliable and prone to errors.

articles.title: Three dead in suspected hantavirus outbreak on Atlantic cruise ship | Health News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) confirmed a suspected hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius, a cruise ship sailing from Ushuaia, Argentina to Cape Verde. Three passengers have died, including a 70-year-old man who died on board and his 69-year-old wife who passed away in a Johannesburg hospital after being evacuated. At least five other passengers are suspected of being infected.  The WHO is coordinating with countries to evacuate the two remaining passengers showing symptoms.

articles.title: Healthcare federation welcomes relaxation of construction rules - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: NATHEALTH, the Healthcare Federation of India, has welcomed the notification of the National Building Construction Standards (NBCS) 2026. The new rules will allow hospitals to establish intensive care units beyond 45 meters in height, subject to enhanced fire safety provisions. Sangita Reddy, president of NATHEALTH and joint managing director of Apollo Hospitals Group, praised the move as a significant step towards future-ready healthcare infrastructure in India.  Varun Khanna, Vice President of NATHEALTH and group managing director of Quality Care India Ltd., also highlighted the potential for unlocking capacity more efficiently and optimizing cost benefits for patients.

articles.title: Three passengers dead after suspected hantavirus outbreak on cruise ship | Cape Verde | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A suspected hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius, a polar cruise ship operated by Oceanwide Expeditions, has resulted in three deaths. The outbreak began onboard the ship, which was traveling between Argentina and Cape Verde, with one confirmed case and five suspected cases reported to the World Health Organization.  The ship's passengers have been evacuated to South Africa for treatment, while two other sick passengers are being considered for isolation. The UK’s Foreign Office is monitoring the situation and stands ready to support British nationals.

articles.title: Three dead in suspected hantavirus outbreak on Atlantic cruise ship
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) has confirmed one case of Hantavirus on a cruise ship sailing in the Atlantic Ocean, with five suspected cases under investigation. Three people, including two passengers from South Africa and a British national, have died after the outbreak aboard the MV Hondius, which departed from Argentina on March 20th and was expected to arrive in Cape Verde on May 4th.  Oceanwide Expeditions, the cruise ship operator, is working with WHO to manage the situation and evacuate passengers.

articles.title: 13-year-old school girl dies of heart attack in Uttara Kannada - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Gangu Gavali, a 13-year-old seventh-grade student, died of a heart attack in Chapeli-Gavaliwada village near Joida, Uttara Kannada district on Sunday (May 3, 2026).  The girl had no known medical conditions and was playing games the day before her death. She woke up vomiting and collapsed shortly after, according to her parents who reported the incident to the police. Officers from the Ramanagar police station are investigating the cause of death.

articles.title: Concern for jailed Iranian Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi as family say health deteriorating
articles.rephrased_article: Narges Mohammadi, a Nobel Peace Prize laureate and human rights activist, has been transferred to a hospital in Zanjan province following a reported deterioration of her health. Her family expressed concern over the lack of adequate medical care she received while imprisoned, citing her history of cardiac, lung, and blood pressure problems. The Narges Mohammadi Foundation, run by her family, called for her transfer to a Tehran hospital where specialists could provide proper treatment.  Jorgen Watne Frydnes, head of the Nobel Peace Prize committee, also expressed concern about her life-threatening situation.

articles.title: Tele-MANAS helpline counselling 3,000 people per month in A.P., says Health Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Minister for Health, Family Welfare and Medical Education Satya Kumar Yadav stated that the Tele-MANAS helpline, launched by the Union government in 2022 to address mental health issues, is providing support to individuals experiencing stress, depression, and anxiety. The national helpline, operated by NIMHANS, Bengaluru, routes calls to call centers within each state, with two centers in Andhra Pradesh located in Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam.

articles.title: Health Dept. suspends two faculty members in sexual harassment case - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Dr. Nori Ramasastry Government Ayurvedic Medical College Principal K. Nirmala Jyothibai
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare suspended Assistant Professor D. Mouli Naik, a laboratory technician K. V. Subrahmanyam, and removed Dr. Nori Ramasastry Government Ayurvedic Medical College Principal K. Nirmala Jyothibai and Professor K. Vijayakumari from their positions for alleged sexual harassment of a student at the college in Vijayawada.  AYUSH In-charge Commissioner Ronanki Gopalakrishna stated that further investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: Karnataka launches divisional drive to integrate TB and tobacco control programmes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Karnataka launched a divisional-level initiative to integrate tuberculosis control and tobacco cessation services, bringing together the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP) and the National Tobacco Control Programme (NTCP).  The State Tobacco Control Cell, in partnership with Vital Strategies, convened a workshop in Bengaluru to operationalize the TB-Tobacco Integration Framework across nine districts. The initiative aims to address the significant link between tobacco use and tuberculosis, particularly highlighting the increased risk of developing active TB and treatment failure for tobacco users. Participants were trained on the Ask-Advise-Refer (AAR) brief intervention model and prepared district action plans for implementing standard operating procedures and staff training within a month.

articles.title: Crisis in Sindh health department as 75pc of top-level technical posts lying vacant - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sindh's health department is facing a severe shortage of top-level technical experts, with over 75% of Grade-20 posts in the health management cadre vacant. This critical gap has left the province vulnerable to outbreaks of infectious diseases like mpox, measles, malaria, and dengue.  The health department acknowledges the issue and plans to expedite promotions for existing officers while also recruiting new doctors at lower grades.

articles.title: World’s rarest hybrid blood type discovered in Thailand: Study found in just 3 people out of a massive research of 544,000 samples | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers in Thailand examined over half a million blood samples and discovered a rare "hybrid-like" blood type, the B(A) phenotype.  This unusual finding was identified through routine screening work and only appeared in three individuals out of the large sample set. Experts suggest this discovery highlights that standard blood tests might not fully capture all variations within the ABO system. The study published in *Transfusion and Apheresis Science* suggests that more hidden blood types could exist, especially in diverse populations.

articles.title: First malaria drug for babies is approved in ‘major public health milestone’ | Global development | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization has approved Coartem Baby, a new malaria treatment for infants, marking a significant advancement in combating the disease. The drug, developed by Novartis and the Medicines for Malaria Venture (MMV), can be used on babies as small as 2kg and comes in sweet cherry-flavored tablets that dissolve easily into liquids. This approval is expected to significantly reduce infant malaria deaths, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa where up to 18% of children under six months are infected. The Gates Foundation is among the donors supporting MMV's efforts to develop safe and effective treatments for malaria.

articles.title: Pakistan Medical Association warns of ‘man-made epidemic’ over syringe reuse - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Medical Association (PMA) has called for a nationwide audit of syringe manufacturing units and the seizure of non-compliant stocks, blaming the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (Drap) and provincial health authorities for a "catastrophic failure" that has led to widespread use of reusable syringes despite a ban. The association also urged an emergency awareness campaign to educate the public on identifying genuine auto-disable syringes and called for stringent legal action against clinics and practitioners using banned conventional syringes.  The PMA expressed concern over the rise in HIV cases, attributing it to substandard equipment and warned that without immediate intervention, this could evolve into a national emergency.

articles.title: US court limits mail-order access to abortion pill mifepristone
articles.rephrased_article: The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals has temporarily reinstated a requirement that abortion pills be obtained in person, significantly restricting access to the medication by mail. This decision overturns a 2023 FDA regulation allowing doctors to send pills without in-person visits and is seen as a setback for reproductive rights advocates. The ruling was celebrated by Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill, while New York Attorney General Letitia James stated that abortion access will remain legal in her state.  The decision has drawn criticism from organizations like the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), who argue it undermines women's health and access to vital care.

articles.title: ‘Sustainable healthcare practices key to future’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Raj Narayan Tiwari, director of the Indian Council of Medical Research, National Institute for Research in Environmental Health, Bhopal, urged graduating medical students from the Kodagu Institute of Medical Sciences to adopt sustainable practices and act as environmental conservation ambassadors. He emphasized the importance of compassion, empathy, research, and community medicine in achieving India's vision of becoming a developed nation by 2047.  T.M. Dharmaja Uthappa, KIMS director and dean, also advised graduates to uphold the dignity of their profession.

articles.title: Australia wants to be first nation in the world to eliminate a cancer - can it?
articles.rephrased_article: Australia is on track to eliminate cervical cancer by 2035, a goal that has been made possible through its successful vaccination and screening programs. The country's efforts have been lauded as a global exemplar for other nations seeking to eradicate the disease.  However, challenges remain in achieving full elimination, particularly among Indigenous communities who face higher rates of cervical cancer and mortality. Professor Karen Canfell, an epidemiologist leading the effort, emphasizes that while Australia has made significant progress, continued investment in vaccination programs and addressing healthcare disparities is crucial for success.

articles.title: Doctors’ body seeks cap on duty hours, flags 36-hour shifts for Telangana resident PG doctors - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Healthcare Reforms Doctors Association (HRDA) in Telangana has written to the Director of Medical Education (DME) urging the implementation of regulated duty hours for resident doctors, senior residents, and interns. The association cites national standards and reports highlighting the negative impact of excessive working hours on trainee well-being, patient safety, and healthcare quality. They have requested the DME to issue directions mandating a maximum 12-hour shift and 48-hour workweek with weekly offs for all medical colleges in the state.

articles.title: Doctors’ body seeks cap on duty hours, flags 36-hour shifts for Telangana resident PG doctors - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Healthcare Reforms Doctors Association (HRDA) in Telangana has written to the Director of Medical Education (DME) requesting the implementation of regulated duty hours for resident doctors, senior residents, and interns across government and private medical colleges. The association cited national standards and reports highlighting the detrimental effects of excessive working hours on trainee well-being, patient safety, and healthcare quality.  The HRDA urged the DME to issue directions mandating a maximum of 12-hour shifts and 48-hour workweeks with weekly off days for all medical colleges in the state.
